author: Francesco Mattana
title: Torta Caprese - Italian Chocolate and Almond Cake
ingredients: The zest of ½ an orange
instructions_list: Over a bain marie, gently melt the butter and chocolate, stirring continuously until it's completely melted and silky. Set aside to cool.
Meanwhile separate the egg yolks from the egg whites. Whisk the egg yolks with ⅔ of the sugar until creamy and thick, then add this to the melted chocolate and butter.
Add the orange zest, vanilla paste and almond flour then mix together until everything is well incorporated.
Whisk the egg whites with the remaining sugar until stiff peaks form. Then fold the egg whites into the chocolate mix.

Grease a 22cm cake tin with butter and then dust it with almond flour, making sure to reach all the corners. Pour the cake mix into the tin, spread it evenly and bake at 170°C static or 150°C fan for 40-45 minutes. You can check it's ready by inserting a toothpick or wooden skewer into the middle of the cake. It should come out with a few moist crumbs attached, not wet, gooey batter.

Rest the cake for 1 hour and a half or until fully cool. Take it out of the tin (or flip it over and then flip it again so the base of the cake is again at the bottom of the plate) and allow it to cool completely. Dust generously with icing sugar and serve.
description: Torta Caprese is a traditional Italian chocolate and almond cake that comes from the island of Capri in Naples. It’s very easy-to-make and it's naturally gluten-free! This cake is nutty, chocolatey and rich, with a hint of sweetness from the vanilla and citrus from the orange. In Italy we love to eat this cake for breakfast alongside a nice espresso but it can also be enjoyed as a snack at any time of the day or as a dessert.
